narrative:
The model predicts an 86% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon, based on patterns from many similar employees.

The three factors that most influenced this decision were your overall years of experience, the time you have spent in your current role, and whether you have received other job offers. Your 11+ years of total experience was the strongest driver pushing the prediction toward leaving. While only 15% of employees the model expects to stay have this much experience, the pattern shows that people with very long careers often explore new opportunities. Your 1-5 years in this organization was the second-biggest factor and also pulled the prediction toward leaving; most people the model thinks will stay have either much shorter or noticeably longer tenure here. Finally, the fact that you have received other job offers was the third most important reason, strongly increasing the likelihood of departure because external opportunities frequently lead to actual exits.

Taken together, these signals suggest you may be ready for a change. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly. You might consider what would make staying worthwhile, while the company could explore whether additional responsibilities or changes in role could meet your needs before you decide to move on.
